# Real deepest-face plateaus and common-cap section barycenter bodies
It gives exact real-base contact geometry and packages the already proved
one-cap zonoid condition as a compact convex set of possible anchors.
It does not create signed compatible body variations or prove OC.

The ordinary own-depth-root contact theorem in
candidate 4202609a15fa8f99
concerns a different measure at each fiber. Here depth always uses the
ONE original full mixed measure, even at a point with noninteger base.

## 1. Exact plateau over every real point of a witness face

Use the positive mixed-volume setting and notation of
fixed-parity-face-witnesses-and-all-circuit-protecting-cones-coherent.md.
Let I be the complete set of deepest integer bases, Q its raw depth,
and F a maximal measured minimal face of conv(I), with witness
p in relint F intersect I.

For every REAL z in F, the maximum raw ambient depth among points
of the actual section C_z is exactly Q.

Indeed z is a convex combination of vertices of F, which are
members of I. The same combination of deepest points at those
vertices belongs to C_z and has depth at least Q, by convexity
of depth superlevel sets. Conversely any critical circuit at
the witness covers the entire continuous plane over F with
caps each of mass Q. Every point over z is therefore in a
Q-budget cap, giving the reverse bound.

Let T_F be the set of all depth-Q points over F. It is nonempty
over every z in F and is convex. For EVERY critical circuit
at p, every point of T_F lies on EVERY cap plane of that
circuit. A positive margin would permit a small threshold
increase retaining that point and removing positive mass
from the cap's proper anchor section. All margins are
therefore nonpositive. Their positive weighted sum is zero
over F, so every margin is zero.

## 2. The exact affine contact flat

Take the union of the continuous normals of all critical
circuits at p, and let r be the rank of their span. Choose
r independent normals u_1,...,u_r from this union, with
their actual cap equations

    u_j.x=b_j-a_j.z.

Let U be the r by d matrix of these rows, let A have rows
a_j, and let b have coordinates b_j. Put

    x_0(z)=U^T(UU^T)^(-1)(b-Az),      W=ker U.          (1)

The full common intersection of ALL these cap equations,
over aff F, is exactly

    { (z,x_0(z)+w): z in aff F, w in W }.              (2)

To check the extra equations, any additional continuous
normal is a linear combination of the chosen rows. The
corresponding affine equation is consistent at every z
in F, because T_F has a point over every such z. After
subtracting that row combination, its residual is an
affine base function vanishing on F, hence on aff F.
This proves (2).

If r=d, every deepest lift over F is unique and equals
(z,x_0(z)); its existence proves that this affine point
actually belongs to C_z for every z in F. In particular
its integer-base points belong to S.

If r<d, (2) is ONLY a containing solution flat. It does
not assert that x_0(z) itself belongs to C_z, that every
point of C_z in the flat is deepest, or that the deepest
sets have an affine selection inside them.

The shear (z,x)->(z,x-x_0(z)) preserves the integer base
coordinate, translates every continuous fiber, preserves
all mixed fiber volumes, and sends halfspaces to halfspaces.
It is therefore an allowed lattice-preserving normalization.
On F, every selected critical cap then has trace u.x>=0.
No compatibility slack follows from this flattening.

## 3. A common regular cap can have only one minimizing anchor

Fix any nonvertical cap H of mass Q which is critical at
an interior anchor y. Normalize its continuous normal to
unit length. Let theta_P be its summed proper-section
measure in full physical coordinates w=(z,x), and let
A=theta_P(total)>0.

If every supporting section on its boundary has zero
(d-1)-measure, varying the FULL ambient normal by e while
keeping the cap through y has derivative

    integral e.(w-y) dtheta_P(w).

This is the ordinary proper-section slab formula; supporting
sections of zero area contribute o(t). Both signs of the
variation are permitted and H is a minimizing cap at y,
so the derivative vanishes for every e. Consequently

    y=(1/A) integral w dtheta_P.                       (3)

The right side is fixed by H, and includes the integer
coordinates as well as the continuous coordinates.
Thus this one regular cap cannot be minimizing at two
distinct physical points, even at different real bases.

In fact the absence of EMPTY-side supporting facets is
enough. The audited one-cap zonoid condition in
candidate 9c6d3cb586898f7e
shows that absence of such facets also removes all
FULL-side supporting facets and gives (3).

Therefore if F has positive dimension, EVERY witness
critical cap has a positive-measure empty-side supporting
section somewhere in the original measured fibers. The
same conclusion holds if there are two distinct deepest
points over a single base.

This is the fixed-face application of the archived
facet-free and orientation-resolved contact facts, not
a newly claimed regularity theorem. Entirely transverse
critical-circuit menus cannot exist at positive-dimensional
witness faces. On the other hand, special restricted
variation spaces can still have linear quantile responses
despite supporting coincidences; that possibility is not
discarded.

## 4. Compact convex bodies of possible section barycenters

The exact nonsmooth replacement for (3) has a useful
finite-measure description. Let theta_E and theta_F
be the section measures on empty-side and full-side
supporting faces of this fixed cap. Zero-area sections
are omitted without changing any derivative. All these
measures have compact support on the cap plane.

For any nonzero finite positive measure L and any finite
positive measure E on a common compact set, define

    B(L,E)={
       [integral w dL + integral w alpha(w)dE]
           /[L(total)+integral alpha(w)dE]:
                              0<=alpha<=1 Borel }.      (4)

This is a compact convex set. Compactness follows from
weak compactness of measures alpha E dominated by E
and continuity of their masses and first moments; the
denominator is bounded below by L(total)>0.
For convexity, if densities alpha_1,alpha_2 give masses
T_1,T_2 and barycenters y_1,y_2, choose

    a=t T_2/[t T_2+(1-t)T_1].

The density a alpha_1+(1-a)alpha_2 is admissible and its
barycenter is t y_1+(1-t)y_2. This proves convexity,
including t=0 or 1 by the endpoint conventions.

For any linear functional u, the upper support value
R=h_(B(L,E))(u) is the unique real solution of

    integral (u.w-R)dL
       +integral (u.w-R)_+ dE=0.                      (5)

The left side is continuous and strictly decreasing,
with slope decrease at least L(total), and tends to
opposite infinities at the two ends. For any alpha,
the numerator minus R times the denominator of (4)
is at most the left side of (5). Equality is attained
by alpha=1_(u.w>R). Thus (5) gives exactly the maximum,
not merely a bound. The lower endpoint is the analogous
root with the negative part min(u.w-R,0).

## 5. Exact relation to one-cap stationarity

Let Y_H be the set of points y on the cap plane for
which every first-order cap-normal variation through y
has nonnegative directional mass derivative. Then

    Y_H=intersection_(0<=alpha_F<=1)
                 B(theta_P+alpha_F theta_F, theta_E). (6)

To verify this, the audited zonoid condition says that
for EVERY prescribed alpha_F there is alpha_E in [0,1]
such that

    integral (w-y)dtheta_P
      +integral alpha_F(w)(w-y)dtheta_F
      +integral alpha_E(w)(w-y)dtheta_E=0.

Since the mandatory proper mass A is positive, this
identity is exactly y belonging to the corresponding
barycenter body in (6). Conversely those identities
for every alpha_F give the zonoid inclusion, equivalent
to all one-sided first-order cap-normal inequalities.

Thus Y_H is compact and convex. Every actual minimizing
anchor of H belongs to it, so in particular T_F is
contained in Y_H for every witness critical cap.
Membership in Y_H is only FIRST-ORDER stationarity; it
is not asserted to make H a global minimizing cap.

Equation (6) preserves the original quantifiers. The
empty-side density can depend on the prescribed
full-side density and on y. No common allocation is
being imposed.

## 6. A quantitative width bound with a mandatory section mass

Let A=L(total)>0 and B=E(total), and let K be the
compact convex hull of the supports of L and E.
Every probability law in (4) dominates the SAME
subprobability measure

    L/(A+B),

whose mass is A/(A+B). Indeed its actual denominator
is A+integral alpha dE<=A+B. The residual probability
mass is B/(A+B), and it is supported in K. Therefore
the barycenter set (4) satisfies the directional bound

    width_u B(L,E)
        <= [B/(A+B)] width_u K.                       (7)

This proof uses one common submeasure for ALL choices
of alpha; it does not select incompatible endpoint
allocations and then equate them.

Applying only alpha_F=0 in (6) gives the useful
necessary estimate for any common deepest face:

    width_u T_F
       <= [theta_E(total)/(theta_P(total)+theta_E(total))]
          width_u conv(supp theta_P union supp theta_E).         (8)

The other prescribed full-side densities in (6) can
only make its containing region smaller.

The width estimate is compatible with the archived
orientation-resolved exterior-facet flux inequality.
It is a barycenter-body formulation of that local
constraint, not a proof that the empty-side section
mass is bounded by the OC cap budget.

## 7. An affine deepest graph does not create independent fiber motions

The actual source in
candidate 5cb6b3de949f5208
has d=1 and

    C={-1<=q<=1, |p|<=4-3q,
                      |x|<=8/5+(3/5)q}.

Its exact deepest points are

    (-1,0,0), (0,0,0), (1,0,0),

all of raw depth 24 and normalized depth 1/3. Those
facts, including every oblique cap, are proved in that
source and its independent audit. The two common
critical caps x+q>=0 and -x+q>=0 have full continuous
normal span. The present theorem consequently gives
the entire real deepest graph

    {(p,0,0):-1<=p<=1}

over its maximal measured face.

Nevertheless each of the three deepest integer fibers
is completely locked if all other fibers are fixed.
All q=0 fibers for integer p=-4,...,4 equal the same
interval K=[-8/5,8/5]. If only the fiber at an interior
index p in {-1,0,1} is replaced by L, actual convexity
at target p gives

    K=(K_(p-1)+K_(p+1))/2 subset L.

Actual convexity at target p+1, with sources p and p+2,
gives

    (L+K)/2 subset K.

Support functions then imply h_L<=h_K in both continuous
directions, hence L subset K. Thus L=K.

So neither the real plateau nor the full-rank affine
contact graph supplies any nontrivial independent
signed deformation of a deepest fiber. Coupled changes
may still be possible. The example is above the OC
target and is not asserted to be a local minimum among
all bodies; it does not obstruct a descent theorem
that uses the below-target hypothesis essentially.

The remaining global issue is unchanged: these contact
and section laws constrain critical caps, while compatible
body motions and the sign of their full cap budgets
require an additional argument.

## 8. A finite geometric circuit menu in a precisely scoped polyhedral case

There is a useful finiteness consequence, with stronger hypotheses
than the preceding sections. Suppose all positive fibers are polytopes,
dim F>=1, and

    aff F=aff P,

where P is the complete set of positive measured bases. Only the
critical circuits at the chosen witness p are considered. Let r be
their continuous-normal rank as in Section 2. After the same permitted
shear, EVERY cap in EVERY such circuit agrees, on the entire measured
affine space aff(P) x R^d, with a halfspace

    u.x>=0.                                             (9)

Indeed its cap equation already has this form on F; its remaining
base-affine term vanishes on F, hence on aff(P). No full-rank assumption
r=d or actual affine selection inside the fibers is needed for this
statement. Components of an ambient integer normal perpendicular to
aff(P) may differ, but they do not change any measured cap trace.

By Section 3, every such cap has an empty-side positive-area supporting
section on some measured fiber. Thus its continuous unit normal u is
an outward facet normal of one of the finitely many sheared fiber
polytopes. More precisely that facet lies on u.x=0 and its fiber is
contained in u.x<=0. In dimension d=1 the two interval endpoints are
the facets, with H_0 section measure; the same assertion holds.

Consequently there are only FINITELY MANY distinct cap traces that
can occur in these witness circuits. They can be listed explicitly:
take the distinct continuous unit outward normals of all fiber
facets whose supporting plane has height zero, form (9), and retain
only those with actual mixed cap mass Q whose plane passes through
one chosen actual deepest lift at the witness. Every retained cap
is then active there. A minimal positive dependence among retained
normals gives a critical circuit; Section 1 consequently shows that
its caps pass through every deepest lift at the witness. Conversely
every witness critical circuit appears on this finite list. Retained
caps which occur in no positive circuit may simply be discarded.

Make that discard before defining N as the number of distinct retained
normals. Every remaining normal is then in the rank-r span from
Section 2. The number of
minimal circuit subsets is at most

    sum_(j=2)^(r+1) binomial(N,j).                       (10)

To justify the size bound, a support-minimal positive dependence
has one-dimensional linear dependency space and rank j-1: a second
independent relation would allow the positive coefficients to be
perturbed until a coefficient vanished, contradicting minimality.
All selected normals lie in the rank-r span. Repeated caps may be
grouped; each minimal subset has one positive dependence up to scale.

Every empty-side donor base in this argument lies OUTSIDE F. An
integer base in F belongs to I by completeness of the deepest-base
set, and its deepest lift is interior to its positive fiber. A common
cap passes through that lift, so cuts that fiber properly and cannot
support it on either side. This excludes all facet donors in F,
including its boundary integer points.

In particular, in this scoped situation P cannot be contained in F:
otherwise there would be no required empty-side donor at all. This
last observation does not exclude product cube examples, whose
maximal measured minimal faces have dimension zero and whose convex
hull has no relative-interior integer witness.

The finiteness here concerns GEOMETRIC CAPS AND CIRCUITS, not their
body-variation responses. Supporting coincidences are compulsory,
and the permitted full-side and empty-side allocation functions can
still form infinite-dimensional families. Thus no finite list of
linear gradients, common multiplier certificate, signed variation
space, or numerical OC bound is inferred from (9)--(10).
